Shanghai/Ningbo.note: Both halves reopened on 28 Aug. SIPG restarted Waigaoqiao empty gates and Yangshan laden gates at 12:00 HKT and Yangshan empty gates at 14:00 HKT; Ningbo-Zhoushan terminals resumed laden and empty gate-in and pick-up at 15:00 HKT, with yards back at 12:00 and warehouses at 08:00. Ningbo stepped its emergency response down from Level I to Level II, Shanghai holds at Level II. Landside is moving again but the water side is not: SEKO puts berth waits at 9+ days for WGQ2 and WGQ5, 7+ days at Yangshan Phase 1-2, and 5-6 days across Ningbo as bunched vessels come back in. Yard occupancy is Waigaoqiao 76%, Yangshan 1-2 85%, Ningbo MSICT 95% with other Ningbo terminals near 92%. Expect heavy roll-overs through Weeks 35 and 36.

Xiamen.note: Xiamen came through the watch period essentially untouched. Toll's local team reported no impact to port operations on 26 Aug, and SEKO on 28 Aug has Xiamen stabilising as vessel tie-downs are cleared and feeder connections progressively restart. Saudel made landfall to the north on the Zhejiang-Fujian border and is tracking inland to the west, so the threat to Fujian is over. Marked as ended 28 Aug — this entry clears itself in two days.

remarks: Saudel is finished as a weather event. JMA has it down to a tropical depression at 27N 116E over central-southern China, 996 hPa, running west at 30 km/h, and the 29 Aug 03:50 JST bulletin carries no forecast track — it should drop out of the feed within a day. What it left behind is the story now.

Shanghai/Ningbo is the one that matters. It reopened on 28 Aug but sits on 1.53m TEU at anchorage and a queue-to-berth ratio of 2.68 on the 23 Aug Linerlytica snapshot, and that was before the shutdown. Berth waits of 9+ days at Waigaoqiao on top of a backlog never fully cleared from Typhoon Dolphin earlier in the month means this queue gets worse before it gets better.
Shanghai/Ningbo moves from suspended to recovering this run. That also switches off the site's 'berths idle' flag for the pair, which is correct now that the gates are open.

Xiamen is dropped from watch with an end date of 28 Aug. It never actually closed — 27,320 TEU at anchorage and a 0.29 ratio on the latest snapshot is a quiet roadstead. Saudel is still inside 600 km of it and of Shenzhen, but as a decaying depression over land, so both rank as watch only.

Bang-lang has been upgraded to a severe tropical storm and named since the last run, and Etau is still out there, but both are near Wake Island, 3,300 km from the nearest tracked port. Neither is a threat this week.

Qingdao is worth a mention without an entry: SEKO logs a 21-hour closure on 24 Aug from rough seas, but waits are back to 1-1.5 days and the only live constraint is maintenance dredging at QQCTU blocking one berth through mid-September. That is routine, not an event.
Yantian's 5-6 day waits for mega vessels are chronic congestion ahead of Golden Week, not weather. Not logged as a port event.
